column3: BootUI 2.4.0 RuntimeJournal.addListener makes aggregate registration idempotent (no-op on duplicate, preserving counts and coverage). In sharpit, RuntimeJournal has no drain thread or listener dispatch; HookRegistry registers capture hooks idempotently by name, and RuntimeJournal exposes no listener registration API, preventing duplicate registration by design. Ported as guard in test_registering_the_same_aggregate_again_neither_counts_twice_nor_repairs_missing_coverage.

BootUI 2.4.0 #1598 adds rememberCompletedExecution and a bounded expired-id set to JournalAggregates (JournalAggregatesTests.completedExecutionAttributesLateSqlToItsCompletedWork and two siblings). sharpit keeps no running aggregates and no producer sets executionId: SQL and connection events join their request by requestId at read time (engine/collectors/insights/requests.py), so a late event lands on its own request or stays unattributed and never opens an execution. Port with the aggregates if sharpit gains them.

BootUI 2.4.0 orders the request-profile timeline by offsetMillis, then SQL execution start, then sequence (RequestJournalProfiles.java; RequestJournalProfilesTests.delayedSqlTimelineTiesUseExecutionStartRatherThanPublicationSequence, sqlMonotonicTieBreakDoesNotMoveItAheadOfNonSqlItems). sharpit's request profile (engine/capture/activity.py request_profile) has no journal timeline yet, so there is nothing to order; the comparator is ported with the timeline (a 0.7.0 gap).
